chunk_findings.detail: On Python 3.12+, f-string contents tokenize as `FSTRING_START`/`FSTRING_MIDDLE`/`FSTRING_END`, not as `tokenize.STRING`. The guard fails, even though no child process is started. Include the f-string token types in the protected set (or otherwise treat them as string regions).

chunk_findings.detail: The tab-column alignment the previous scanner relied on was removed, and the new comment is wrong for the interpreter this test still claims to support. On Python 3.11 `tokenize.generate_tokens` expands each tab to tabsize 8 when it records `(row, column)`, while `spawn.finditer` now runs on the raw line from `src.split("\n")`. Given `ddflow/foo.py` containing `x="\t";subprocess.run([])\n`, the STRING token’s expanded end column runs past the raw index of `subprocess` (string starts at raw column 2; the tab jumps the tokenizer to column 8, so the token ends at column 9, while `m.start()` is 6). The check `start <= (n, m.start()) < end` treats that real call as prose and `continue`s, so the unguarded spawn is never appended to `offenders` and the ratchet passes.

chunk_findings.detail:
By treating every match inside a `STRING` token as non-executable, the ratchet now misses a real unguarded spawn constructed as an evaluated string. For example, a file `ddflow/foo.py` containing
`import subprocess; exec("subprocess.run('echo hi')")`
has its `subprocess.run` occurrence inside a `STRING` token, so `any(start <= (n, m.start()) < end ...)` skips it and no offender is recorded. That module does spawn a child without going through `proc`, which is exactly the invariant this test exists to enforce; the old `spawn.search(line)` would have reported it.

    def test_every_guard_has_its_own_baseline_file_and_nothing_else_is_there() -> None:
        """One file per guard (a directory of files, one per module, for the PER_MODULE
        counters): each counter and each `.importlinter` contract has its baseline
        file, holding exactly its keys; `.importlinter` itself lists no allowlist (two homes
        for one list would drift); and no other file is there -- one left behind by a renamed
        or removed guard would be read by nothing while looking like it still guarded."""

chunk_findings.detail: The test never calls `run_cli(repo, "init")` before its first command `run_cli(repo, "task", "add", "H1", ...)`. The neighboring test `test_an_exact_file_the_holder_claimed_is_never_free` explicitly calls `run_cli(repo, "init")` first, which shows the `repo` fixture does not start as an initialized ddflow repository. On a clean test run this test will fail before reaching `AI.update` with a “not a ddflow repository” error, so it is broken on both the unfixed and fixed code.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_glob_update_overlap.py:test_re_stating_a_held_glob_is_not_queued_behind_a_waiter

chunk_findings.detail: `--json update` still cannot be parsed. The bug’s stdout was this function’s prose (`those globs are queued behind …`, `json.load` failing at char 0); lease overlap was cited as the path that already returns a JSON refusal body. The edit only rewrites that same bare string (`f"{item_id}: {named}is queued behind …"`) and still returns it as the refusal. Given `ddflow --json update P-remote.auth --globs …` while a waiter holds one new glob, stdout still starts with the item id, not `{` or `"`, so `json.load` still fails at char 0. No other file in the change switches this return onto the structured refusal used by overlap.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases/lifecycle.py:194

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test does not lock the vague-refusal half of the bug. It only asserts a re-stated `README.md` plus `other.py` succeeds, so it stays green if the refusal text is reverted to `those globs are queued behind …` or left non-JSON. The docstring says the refusal must name the file, but the test never drives a real queue conflict (for example adding `changes.toml`, which Q1 already queued) and never checks the body. A naming or JSON regression of `lifecycle.py` is invisible to this test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_glob_update_overlap.py:147

chunk_findings.detail: When `queue_ahead` hits but `WG.conflicts` returns no pairs, `named` is `""` and the sentence is `{item_id}: is queued behind {holder} ({item}), who asked for them first.` That drops the subject and still does not name a glob — the failure mode the bug reported. `reservations._queued_blocker` falls back to `those files are queued behind …`; this path does not. Input: an accepted glob that `queue_ahead` treats as queued while `conflicts(want, ahead.globs, shared)` is empty.
